question: Who was Athaliah's father?
summary: 2 Kings 8:26 and 2 Chronicles 22:2 call Athaliah "the daughter of Omri." 2 Kings 8:18 and 2 Chronicles 21:6 call her "the daughter of Ahab." Omri and Ahab are father and son — one cannot biologically be her father if the other is.

reconcile.connective: Harmonizers read "daughter of Omri" as granddaughter — Athaliah was Ahab's daughter and Omri's granddaughter, so the two titles describe one woman.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells of the Skeptic's Annotated Bible, the source page for this entry, presses that the texts name two different fathers — Omri in 2 Kings 8:26 and 2 Chronicles 22:2, Ahab in 2 Kings 8:18 and 2 Chronicles 21:6 — and that one man cannot be both.

excerpts.excerpt_text: Athaliah the daughter of Omri—more properly, "granddaughter." The expression is used loosely, as the statement was made simply for the purpose of intimating that she belonged to that idolatrous race.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly answers the Omri/Ahab wording: 'daughter of Omri' = granddaughter, used loosely; this is the core harmonization of the named tension.
excerpts.source_note_text:
Forty and two years old was Ahaziah when he began to reign--(Compare Kg2 8:26). According to that passage, the commencement of his reign is dated in the twenty-second year of his age, and, according to this, in the forty-second year of the kingdom of his mother's family [LIGHTFOOT]. "If Ahaziah ascended the throne in the twenty-second year of his life, he must have been born in his father's nineteenth year. Hence, it may seem strange that he had older brothers; but in the East they marry early, and royal princes had, besides the wife of the first rank, usually concubines, as Jehoram had (Ch2 21:17); he might, therefore, in the nineteenth year of his age, very well have several sons" [KEIL] (compare Ch2 21:20; Kg2 8:17).
Athaliah the daughter of Omri--more properly, "granddaughter." The expression is used loosely, as the statement was made simply for the purpose of intimating that she belonged to that idolatrous race.
